findings.title: Dynamic imports are triggered eagerly, defeating the purpose of async/lazy loading
findings.body: Every property in the appStore object literal calls `import("./appName")` directly as part of module evaluation. Because these import() calls are not wrapped in a function/getter, they execute as soon as `packages/app-store/index.ts` is first required, i.e. all 29 app packages begin loading immediately, exactly like the previous eager `import * as` style, just now wrapped in Promises. Any code path that imports `appStore` (which includes almost all booking/calendar/payment code) will kick off every app's dynamic import regardless of which app is actually needed, so there is no genuine code-splitting/lazy-loading benefit, while every consumer now pays the extra cost of awaiting a Promise. To actually get on-demand loading, each entry would need to be a function (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) invoked only when a specific app key is accessed.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) inside try/catch cannot catch async errors — unhandled rejections and lost error logging
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is wrapped in a try/catch intended to log errors via `logger.error`, but `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the promise returned by its async callback and never awaits it. Since `getCalendar` is now async and awaited inside this callback, any rejection (e.g. from `getCalendar` or `calendar.deleteEvent`) happens asynchronously after `forEach` has already returned, so the surrounding try/catch never sees it — the error is silently swallowed as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged, and the function can return `true` before the calendar/video cleanup has actually completed or even been attempted successfully.

findings.title: Same forEach(async ...) try/catch defect as vital/lib/reschedule.ts
findings.body: Identical to the vital/lib/reschedule.ts issue: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is inside a try/catch block that cannot catch rejections thrown by the async callback because forEach doesn't await it. Errors from the now-async `getCalendar` call (or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting) are not logged and the function can resolve before cleanup finishes.

findings.title: Recurring-event calendar deletion still uses unfixed forEach(async ...), unlike the sibling block fixed a few lines below
findings.body: In the recurring-events branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` pushes results into `apiDeletes` asynchronously, but nothing awaits the promise returned by each forEach callback. Meanwhile the `else` branch directly below (lines ~476-484) was converted in this same PR to a proper `for...of` loop with `await`, showing the author was aware of the pattern but didn't apply the same fix here. As a result, `apiDeletes` may not contain all pending deletions by the time it is passed into `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` later in the function, so some calendar-deletion calls run detached from the request's awaited work and their completion/errors are not guaranteed to be captured before the handler responds.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) with no awaiting or error handling for calendar/video cleanup during reschedule
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` now performs an `await getCalendar(...)` inside an async callback that forEach never awaits and that has no surrounding try/catch. Any failure in `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the subsequent code (sending the reschedule email, firing webhooks) proceeds without waiting for these calendar/video cleanup operations to finish or succeed.

findings.title: No tests added/updated for the new async appStore contract
findings.body: This PR changes the fundamental contract of `appStore` from a synchronous object of modules to an object of Promises, requiring every consumer to `await appStore[key]` (and `getCalendar`, `getVideoAdapters`, etc. to become async). Several call sites across the codebase needed manual fixes in this very PR (some still incomplete, e.g. forEach(async...) patterns). No tests were added to verify that all current and future consumers correctly await these values, leaving the change prone to silent regressions where a missed `await` returns a Promise where a `Calendar`/`VideoApiAdapter` instance was expected.
